plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked ATP hydrolysis energy & Szent-Györgyi actomyosin contraction chart from Lohmann (August 1929, Naturwissenschaften 17: 624–625), Fiske & SubbaRow (October 1929, Science 70: 381–382), Engelhardt & Lyubimova (1939, Nature 144: 668–669), and Szent-Györgyi (1942) shows ATP splitting into ADP + Pi (~30.5 to 50 kJ/mol released) to drive actomyosin thread superprecipitation and contraction, with the human body holding ~50–100 g of ATP and recycling ~50–75 kg/day.

teach_overlay.detail: Inked ATP hydrolysis energy & Szent-Györgyi actomyosin contraction chart on period paper from Lohmann (August 1929, Naturwissenschaften 17: 624–625), Fiske & SubbaRow (October 1929, Science 70: 381–382), Engelhardt & Lyubimova (1939, Nature 144: 668–669), and Szent-Györgyi (1942) showing ATP splitting into ADP + Pi (~30.5 to 50 kJ/mol released) to drive actomyosin thread superprecipitation and contraction, with the human body holding ~50–100 g of ATP and recycling ~50–75 kg/day
teach_overlay.scale: your body holds only about fifty grams of ATP at any one moment, yet because every molecule is discharged and recharged nearly a thousand times a day, you burn through your own body weight in ATP every twenty-four hours
